\chapter{Chapter07 — PCPP}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.PCPP}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Nonadaptive string tester]
\lean{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p178-b004}
\label{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester}
For an alphabet $A$ and natural numbers $n$ and $r$, a nonadaptive string tester is a
nonadaptive function tester whose domain is the set of positions $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$
and whose codomain is $A$, with $r$ query positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Local string tester property]
\lean{FABL.IsLocalStringTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b001}
\label{FABL.IsLocalStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsLocalTester, FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester}
Let $A$ be a type with decidable equality, let $n$ be a positive natural number, and let
$r$ be a natural number. For a nonadaptive string tester over $A$ with $n$ positions and
$r$ query positions, a property $P$ of strings in $A^n$, and a real number $[?]$, the
assertion is that this tester is a local tester for $P$ at rate $[?]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Combined input and proof word]
\lean{FABL.inputProofWord}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001
}
\label{FABL.inputProofWord}
\leanok
Let $A$ be an alphabet, let $n$ and $\ell$ be natural numbers, and let $w$ and $q$ be
words of lengths $n$ and $\ell$, respectively. The combined word on the disjoint union
of the input and proof positions agrees with $w$ on input positions and with $q$ on
proof positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Probabilistically checkable proof system]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001
}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester}
For an alphabet $A$ and natural numbers $n$, $\ell$, and $r$, a probabilistically
checkable proof system consists of a nonadaptive function tester with $r$ query
positions whose address domain is the disjoint union of the $n$ input positions and the
$\ell$ proof positions, and whose answers lie in $A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Proof-system acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001
}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.inputProofWord}
Let $A$ be an alphabet, let $n$, $\ell$, and $r$ be natural numbers, and let $V$ be a
probabilistically checkable proof system with these parameters. For an input word
$w\colon\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to A$ and a proof word $q\colon\mathrm{Fin}(\ell)\to A$, the
acceptance probability of $V$ is the probability that its verifier accepts when it is
given the combined input and proof word.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rejection probability]
\lean{FABL.PCPPSystem.rejectionProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001
}
\label{FABL.PCPPSystem.rejectionProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability}
For a PCPP system $V$ with input alphabet $	ext{Alphabet}$, input length $n$, proof
length $ℓ$, and query count $r$, and for an input word $w$ and proof word $\pi$, the
rejection probability is $1$ minus the probability that $V$ accepts $(w,\pi)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[PCPP property]
\lean{FABL.IsPCPP}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001
}
\label{FABL.IsPCPP}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsFar, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability, FABL.PCPPSystem.rejectionProbability}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite alphabet, let $n\ge 1$, and let $V$ be a PCPP system with
input length $n$, proof length $\ell$, and query count $r$. For a property $P$ of
length-$n$ words over $\mathcal A$ and a real number $\rho$, suppose $\rho>0$. Every
word $w$ satisfying $P$ has some proof that $V$ accepts with probability $1$; moreover,
for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, if every word satisfying $P$ is at distance at least
$\varepsilon$ from $w$, then every proof is rejected on $w$ with probability strictly
greater than $\rho\varepsilon$.
\end{definition}

\proofstep
  {FABL.IsPCPP}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001}
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet, let $n\\ge1$, and let $V$ be a probabilistically checkable
proof of proximity system on words of length $n$, with proof length $\\ell$ and a
positive soundness rate $r$. Let $P$ be a property of length-$n$ words, and suppose $V$
has perfect completeness and rejects every word whose relative Hamming distance from
every word satisfying $P$ is greater than any given $\\delta\\in[0,1]$ with probability
strictly greater than $r\\delta$. If a word $w$ and proof cause $V$ to accept with
probability at least $1-r\\varepsilon$ for some $\\varepsilon\\in[0,1]$, then there is a
word satisfying $P$ at relative Hamming distance at most $\\varepsilon$ from $w$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001}
\proofstep
  {FABL.IsPCPP}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001}
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $n>0$, and let $V$ be a
probabilistically checkable proof system for words in $A^n$. Let $P\subseteq A^n$ be a
property and let $r>0$. Suppose every word in $P$ has a proof accepted with probability
$1$. Suppose also that for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, every word $w$, and every proof,
acceptance probability at least $1-r\varepsilon$ implies that some word in $P$ is within
relative Hamming distance $\varepsilon$ of $w$. Then $V$ is a PCPP for $P$ with rate
$r$: for each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, any word at relative Hamming distance greater than
$\varepsilon$ from every word in $P$ is rejected with probability greater than
$r\varepsilon$, for every proof.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Ordered Boolean gates]
\lean{FABL.OrderedBooleanGate}
\label{FABL.OrderedBooleanGate}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, an ordered Boolean gate is either an input bit indexed
by one of the $n$ input positions, a Boolean constant, the negation of an earlier gate,
the conjunction of two earlier gates, or the disjunction of two earlier gates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite Boolean circuit]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p103-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004
}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OrderedBooleanGate}
For a natural number $n$, a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits consists of a finite
number of gates arranged in an order, with each gate either reading an input bit, giving
a Boolean constant, negating an earlier gate, or taking the conjunction or disjunction
of two earlier gates. One gate is distinguished as the output.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Evaluation of a circuit gate]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits, let $x$ be an assignment of Boolean
values to those inputs, and let $i$ be a gate position in $C$. The value of gate $i$ is
obtained by reading the indicated input bit or constant, or by applying its negation,
conjunction, or disjunction to the values of its earlier source gates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit evaluation]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.eval}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b003}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.eval}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.evalGate}
Given a Boolean circuit $C$ on $n$ input bits and an assignment of Boolean values to
those bits, the evaluation of $C$ is the Boolean value at its distinguished output gate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circuit size]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.size}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p104-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004
}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.size}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit}
The size of a Boolean circuit is its number of gates.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accepted inputs]
\lean{FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b003}
\label{FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.eval}
For a Boolean circuit $C$ on $n$ input bits, its accepted property consists of precisely
those inputs on which $C$ evaluates to true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[PCPP description]
\lean{FABL.PCPPDescription}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b001}
\label{FABL.PCPPDescription}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsPCPP, FABL.PCPPSystem}
Let $n\ge1$ and let $P$ be a property of Boolean words of length $n$. A PCPP description
of $P$ specifies a proof length, a query count, a finite PCPP system with Boolean
alphabet and those parameters, and a real rejection rate such that the system has the
PCPP property for $P$ at that rate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Semantic PCPP reduction]
\lean{FABL.SemanticPCPPReduction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004}
\label{FABL.SemanticPCPPReduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty, FABL.PCPPDescription}
A semantic PCPP reduction assigns to every positive input length $n$ and every Boolean
circuit $C$ on $n$ input bits a PCPP description for the property of inputs accepted by
$C$.
\end{definition}
